item.text: The Corruption and Crime Commission evaluated the first two years of WA Police reform following the royal commission's request that it monitor implementation.
item.support: recommended that the Corruption and Crime Commission (the Commission) monitor the implementation of the reform program

item.text: It examined recruitment and training, management, service delivery, complaint investigations and corruption prevention.
item.support: This report is an account and evaluation of measures undertaken by WAPOL to ensure long-term cultural change and improve service delivery.

item.text: The Commission concluded that police had begun reform and strengthened organisational integrity and governance.
item.support: WAPOL has gone some way toward building stronger organisational integrity and sound corporate governance systems and processes.

item.text: It identified continuing challenges in serious complaint investigations, individual performance management, policy development and organisational change.
item.support: The Commission believes WAPOL needs to consider the issues of investigative competence and willingness to fully investigate complaints against police as a priority.

item.quote: There is no doubt that WAPOL has gone some way toward building stronger organisational integrity and sound corporate governance systems and processes.
